label: negative
description: OZ 5 form of N3b-ratelimit-oz4. Same rotateGuardian() rate limit, but guardian/lastRotation live in an ERC-7201 namespaced struct reached through an assembly storage pointer. The require reads $.lastRotation and the body writes $.lastRotation = block.timestamp. The commit REMOVES the rate-limit guard. Rule 3b must NOT fire.
why_labeled: Same false positive as the OZ 4 case (finding 3b-L-ratelimit), exercised through the OZ 5 namespaced-struct init-guard detector. The rate-limit guard reads-and-writes the same namespaced member, matching the one-shot init-guard shape structurally. The discriminator must apply to the namespaced path too: a member counts toward an init guard only if it is written to a compile-time constant somewhere (OZ 5 initializer writes _initialized = 1 through the pointer), which $.lastRotation = block.timestamp never is. Confirmed: the pre-fix rule fires on this before/after pair; the fixed rule must stay quiet.
diff_summary: before.sol -> after.sol: the two-line rate-limit block (the require + `$.lastRotation = block.timestamp`) is removed from rotateGuardian; everything else identical.
